unit.target: Cargo vendor directory creation/configuration and subsequent local-source reuse semantics
unit.action: Inspected exactly the official cargo-vendor command documentation, preserving the prior role-local source-replacement finding only as own-state context.
unit.finding: Cargo documents that cargo vendor places all crates.io and git dependency source trees into the chosen local vendor directory, prints the Cargo configuration needed to use those vendored sources, and treats vendored sources as read-only. The documented example redirects that generated configuration into a Cargo config file. Therefore, once the exact required vendor tree and generated source configuration already exist and are durably present with the project, later source selection can reuse those local vendored sources rather than requiring registry/git source acquisition at use time. The same command documentation also states that --offline prevents Cargo from accessing the network for any reason and restricts it to locally downloaded crates, but this invocation did not execute Cargo or prove an end-to-end build. Creation-time acquisition/provenance of the vendor tree remains separate and unresolved: cargo vendor's purpose is to collect remote dependency sources, and this slice did not establish that initial population can be achieved without prior network access, richer-mode execution, or user execution.
unit.evidence_scope: Official cargo-vendor documentation only: vendor directory contents, emitted configuration for using vendored sources, read-only treatment, the documented config-redirection example, and the command's documented offline option. No Cargo execution, dependency repository, registry, git remote, build, runtime behavior, another version, or second external project was inspected.
source_support: The command vendors all crates.io and git dependencies into the selected directory and states that the completed vendor directory contains the remote dependency sources.
The command prints the configuration needed to use vendored sources and documents redirecting that output into a Cargo config file.
Cargo treats vendored sources as read-only.
The documented --offline option prevents network access and attempts operation using only locally available crates.

scope_guard: This checkpoint establishes documentation-level reuse semantics for an already-populated Cargo vendor directory plus its generated source configuration, and documentation-level no-network behavior of the cargo command's --offline option. It does not establish initial vendor population without network/richer-mode/user execution, exact lockfile closure, checksum completeness, successful cargo build/fetch execution, compilation, runtime behavior, another project/version, or end-to-end richer-mode outcome parity.
residual_uncertainty: Initial creation and provenance of the exact vendor tree without a residual richer-mode or user-execution step remains unverified.
Exact Cargo.lock closure and checksum completeness for a concrete target remain unverified.
No actual cargo build/fetch operation was executed with the vendor configuration and network disabled.
Compilation and runtime behavior remain untested.
End-to-end richer-mode outcome parity remains unverified.
